answer: At its zenith, sybil resistance can mirror CRISPR off-target verification by requiring each agent to prove a unique edit-history signature rather than a claimed identity. Like checking an onyx assay for collateral cuts, the system scores identity provenance against a reference registry, costing attackers repeated costly re-registration to fake clean lineages. A telltale plume of shared micro-signatures flags coordinated fakes, though sophisticated adversaries may mimic legitimate histories, capping detection.
